notes:
Status: closed-lost to OpenAI/Anthropic direct APIs. Short summary of what happened:
- Team had strong product fit for support-agent + reranking; latency targets ~<120ms tail, throughput moderate (200 QPS peak across multi-tenant service).
- Started as well-qualified mid-market opportunity; wanted hosted API to move fast, later asked about Dedicated for predictability.
- POC: seeded with internal tickets; SE Diego ran two-week POC on our hosted API with sample prompt library. Performance looked good; Diego demoed batching and KV cache savings.
- Security: basic SSO/SAML and audit log questions surfaced. They wanted SOC2 and specific data residency notes; security team asked for checklist (shared /drive/security). Not a hard blocker but increased buyer friction.
- Procurement decision: leadership prioritized simplicity and brand familiarity — "we'll go with OpenAI for now, it's simpler and everyone on eng knows the SDKs" (quote from VP Eng 2025-01-23). Anthropic also in shortlist; final decision split between OpenAI (primary) + Anthropic for evaluation.
- Budget: Q1 budget freeze for new vendor commitments; procurement favored continuing with existing OpenAI contract to avoid procurement cycles.
- Internal champion: initial champion (ML lead) left company mid-POC; replacement deprioritized integration. No strong exec sponsor remained.
- Deal reason: combination of brand preference (OpenAI), perceived integration speed, and internal budget freeze. They did not need Redwood's Dedicated or Private features at time of decision.
- Sales posture: low-touch close. Recommend nurture cadence and quarterly check-ins; offer simplified migration guide and cost delta analysis comparing OpenAI per-token cost vs Redwood caching/batching savings.
